rounds.proof_sketch: Input spec fixes dtype=float32. torch.Tensor.float() on a float32 tensor is identity operation (no-op). Removing .float() from float32→float32 conversion produces identical tensor. Range: all float32 values [-inf, inf] including specials → no distinguishing input exists.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes a .float() type conversion call that only has an effect when the input tensor is NOT already float32. Since the input specification explicitly requires dtype=torch.float32 for the positive tensor (arg[1]), calling .float() on it is a no-op - PyTorch returns the same tensor unchanged. The mutated code simply skips this redundant conversion. Both original and mutated versions pass identical float32 tensors to the CUDA kernel, producing bitwise-identical results for any float32 input values. This was confirmed by Layer 2's 112 rounds of testing showing perfect bitwise equivalence.
rounds.kill_strategy: Cannot kill under current contract. Would require changing input dtype to non-float32 (e.g., float16, int64), which violates the fixed dtype=torch.float32 specification. The mutation only affects behavior when input dtype differs from float32.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of type conversion operations like .float(), the testing contract should either explicitly allow dtype variation, or the mutation tool should recognize that removing .float() on inputs constrained to float32 creates an equivalent mutant that should be excluded from coverage metrics.
